claim: Closed shells hold 28.3 L; a bite is 21.2 L at the assumed 75 % fill
law: Two quarter cylinders, V = pi R^2 B / 2
check: claimed 28.3 L, estimate 28.3 L (ratio 1.00)

claim: 3:1 tackle closes the lips with about 1.06 times the line pull
law: Virtual work: line travel / lip travel (frictionless)
check: claimed 1.06 x line pull, estimate 1.06 x line pull (ratio 1.00)

claim: The lips close a full bite in loose saturated sand (force per shell against passive drag at full bite depth)
law: Rankine passive resistance 0.5 gamma' d^2 Kp B, phi' 30 deg, gamma' 10 kN/m3, d = shell radius; virtual work through the 3:1 tackle
check: Drag about 270 N per shell against 350 N per shell with the full grab's submerged weight on the line. Revised after the independent review: closing starts with the grab empty (451 N submerged), sheave friction (three sheaves, 10 to 15 %) is left out, whether 1.06 T acts on each lip or on both is not settled, and denser sand (phi' 40 deg) roughly doubles the drag; the margin lies between about 0.9 and 1.8, so the bite stays open until the test-pit trial

claim: The head's weight opens the shells when the line is slacked on the bottom
law: Single-rope grabs open under their own head weight on slack line; resistance is the shells' pins and the sand lying on the lips
check: head and ballast 14.3 kg; the lips ride up and outward over the surface as they open; confirmed only by a bite trial

claim: The steady pull of the full grab at the capstan stays below the slip clutch's lowest slip
law: Weight of the full grab in air x 1.11 sheave and guide tube friction against the clutch's slip on the third layer at the low end of a +/-5 % setting

claim: The dead-end load indicator shows the highest pull of each lift
law: Hooke's law for a stack of disc springs in series (deflection adds, load is shared); a friction tell-tale on the rod keeps the largest travel
check: Restated for Amish's decision O4 of 2026-10-25: the shear link and its calibrated pin are gone (they were fixed under K1 for true double shear). Fourteen disc springs 18 x 9.2 x 1.0 give about 2.8 mm of rod travel at 1.47 kN on catalogue values to confirm; disc springs have some hysteresis and the tell-tale reads to about one 0.25 kN ring; calibrated on CalRig and checked in the mud at TRL 4

claim: The crank slip clutch caps the capstan pull at the HatchSide tripod's 150 kg rating
law: Friction clutch, T = 2 mu F r_m (two faces, uniform pressure), mu 0.35 for a dry woven facing on ground steel; 4:1 chain; innermost rope layer
check: Restated for Amish's decision O4 of 2026-10-25 (it replaces the 3 mm shear pin, which ran above shear yield in normal hoisting): a 33.8 N m slip from a 1464 N clamp gives 1472 N at the high end of a +/-5 % setting on the first layer. The facing friction moves with moisture and glazing, so the setting rests on CalRig before each campaign and a dry lining inside the guard; in ordinary hoisting it carries about 81% of its slip torque, which a friction face takes without fatigue

claim: The slip window carries the full grab on every rope layer and stays inside the rating
law: One slip torque gives a line pull that falls as the rope builds up on the drum (layer radii 88 to 104 mm); sheave and guide tube friction about 11 %
check: Lowest slip 1127 N (layer 3, low end) against a steady pull of 1068 N, a margin of 1.06; highest 1472 N against the 1472 N rating. A jerked start or breakout suction (about 160 N) makes it slip for a moment and the pawl holds; nothing releases. At +/-10 % the layer 3 low end falls to about 1019 N, under the steady pull, so the narrow window is confirmed on CalRig (TRL 4)

claim: Hoisting power per person is sustainable for a working day
law: Sustained arm cranking by an adult; CAL assumes 50 W each against about 75 W sustained, a figure with no source
check: Revised after the independent review: 75 W is typical of leg pedalling, and sustained arm cranking is nearer 30 to 40 W. At 35 W each the three-person hoist takes about 111 s and the cycle about 3.7 min; with the lead and head sheaves (about 8 %) about 3.3 min at 50 W. A cited arm-crank figure and the timed trial decide; PR-004 is already not met on paper

claim: Crank force for each of two people at the rated grab load
law: Torque balance through the 4:1 chain (95 %) and two bearings (98 %), 250 mm crank, third rope layer; R5 limit 150 N

claim: The band brake holds the drum at the slip clutch's limit
law: Band brake (capstan equation) T1/T2 = e^(mu theta), mu 0.35, 270 deg wrap; 6 kg on a 10.2:1 lever on the band's slack end, the anchored end tight

claim: The band brake holds when the lining is wet or muddy
law: Capstan equation with mu 0.20 to 0.25 for a wet lining
check: Added after the independent review: at mu 0.25 the brake gives about 168 N m and at 0.20 about 117 N m; with the slip clutch of decision O4 the line can apply at most 130 N m (186 N m with the shear pin), so a wet lining at mu 0.20 falls just below it but stays above the 103 N m the 25 m scraper string needs; keep the lining dry and covered, and measure the holding torque wet before use (TRL 4)

claim: The weighted lever applies the brake when it is let go
law: Lever kinematics: the link pin must move away from the band's live end as the weight falls
check: Kit 1.7 model: link pin 25 mm below the pivot on the well side, so the falling weight moved it toward the live end and slackened the band; fixed: pivot lowered to 67 mm, link pin on an upright arm 60 mm above it, link on the band's tangent; ratio about 10.3:1 (CAL uses 10.2)

claim: 8 mm polyester line has an adequate factor on the working pull
law: 12 kN minimum breaking strength, 90 % at the splice; fibre rope slings use 5:1 to 7:1 (EN 1492-4); the reviewer finds catalogue values of 8 to 10 kN, which still give about 7.7

claim: Sheave pitch diameter suits the double-braid line
law: ANSI/ASSP A10.48: at least 6:1 for double-braid rope (Messer 2019)

claim: Fleet angle at the drum keeps the line winding evenly
law: Drum practice: fleet angle about 1.5 to 2 deg or less for a plain drum
check: 1.91 deg <= 2 deg

claim: The line spools evenly over three layers on the plain drum
law: Wire-rope guidance for a smooth drum is about 1.5 deg; multi-layer plain drums usually need grooving or a level wind
check: Added after the independent review: 1.91 deg is over 1.5 deg; the operator guides the line by hand on the third layer; to confirm in the timed trial

claim: The drawbar does not buckle at the slip clutch's limit
law: Euler buckling of a pinned 48.3 x 3.2 tube, E 200 GPa

claim: The capstan does not pitch forward at the slip clutch's limit
law: Overturning couple of rope and drawbar against the capstan's weight about the front rail

claim: The 42.4 x 2.6 pole carries the scraper torque
law: Torsion of a thin tube against shear yield 0.58 x 235 MPa
check: 30 MPa <= 136 MPa

claim: The 25 m scraper string hangs inside the slip clutch's lowest slip on the first layer and the tripod rating
law: String weight x 1.1 against 1,331 N (clutch, innermost layer, low end of the setting) and 1,472 N; sections come off as it rises

claim: Folded, the scraper toes pass the smallest ring bore
law: Four-bar linkage solved in the model; sleeve slides 300 mm on the cross pin
check: 387 mm radius <= 400 mm radius

claim: The scraper arm's pivot eye closes round its 16 mm pin and clears the 70 mm hub
law: An eye needs material round the hole; the hub's radius is the limit
check: Kit 1.7 model: pivot 45 mm from the pole axis, 10 mm outside the hub, so the 50 mm arm ended in an open half hole; fixed: pivot at 60 mm, an 18 mm radius eye clears the hub by 7 mm; toe radius unchanged at 615 mm, fold 387 mm

claim: The 8-ring string sinks 3 m below the water table under its own weight and eight saddles, without de-watering
law: Self-weight against skin friction; skin friction = K sigma'v tan delta for soil in contact (K 0.5, delta 2/3 phi')
check: Sinks only while friction stays below 1.66 kPa (CAL estimate 1 to 3 kPa for disturbed sand); soil in full contact at mid depth gives about 25 kPa, so sinking depends on the 40 mm overcut keeping the soil loose and off the ring. Field practice sinks rings this way with de-watering (Abbott; WaterAid); without it there is no published figure. Revised after the independent review: the central estimate (2 kPa) already exceeds the limit, the overcut is only at the toe and saturated sand closes onto the ring above it, and full contact would need about 270 kN against 18 kN; the claim fails on first order. Decided by Amish on 2026-10-25 (SKG-DEC-001 O2): bentonite slurry fed down a pipe into the overcut annulus is part of the method from the first trial, as in caisson practice and as water-well drillers use bentonite muds. No figure for the lubricated friction is claimed; the test pit must show it below the limit, so the row stays open at TRL 4 and PR-001 is at risk

claim: Sand does not boil into the rings during digging
law: Quick condition needs an upward hydraulic gradient near 1 (Terzaghi); with no de-watering the water inside the rings stands level with the water outside
check: Gradient about zero while the crew does not bail; the grab removes about 21 L a bite, too little to draw the level down. Revised after the independent review: a fast hoist of a sealed grab can draw a transient gradient, and sand can run in under the edge (loss of ground) without boiling; hoist slowly off the bottom and keep the inside level with the outside; to confirm in the trial

claim: Four dip-tape readings resolve tilt finer than the 1 in 80 limit
law: Two readings of +/-3 mm across 1,075 mm (root sum of squares, as CAL I5); resolves the top ring only, so ring flatness and joints add to it

claim: The grab hangs from its line about 8 to 9 degrees out of level
law: A body hung from one point rests with its centre of gravity under that point
check: The line enters the guide tube 65 mm off the grab's axis, about 410 mm above the empty grab's centre of gravity; the grab settles level on the bottom once the line is slack, so the bite is unaffected; no change
closed_by: This file (observation from the detailed model)

claim: Cycle at 10 m with three people at the hoist is about 3.2 min
law: Sum of lowering, crank change, open, close, hoist (50 W each) and dumping
check: claimed 3.2 min, estimate 3.18 min (ratio 1.01)

claim: About 3.6 m3 of soil is removed for 3 m of sinking
law: Cylinder to the toe radius
check: claimed 3.56 m3, estimate 3.56 m3 (ratio 1.00)

claim: The drum holds the line for a 30 m well
law: Turns per layer x pitch circumference over three layers against depth plus reeving and dead turns

claim: Proof load at 1.25 x the rated load is a conservative test for hand-powered lifting gear
law: Static test coefficients in lifting standards are typically 1.25 to 1.5; the applicable standard is to assess (SKG-REG-001)
check: Restated for Amish's decision O4 of 2026-10-25. The independent review found the old basis inconsistent (2 x the link's 122 kg release, 244 kg, exceeded the tripod's 225 kg proof). PR-007 now proofs at 1.25 x the rated load, the clutch's highest slip (150 kg): 188 kg, inside the HatchSide proof, with the clutch locked out for the test. 1.25 sits at the low end of static test coefficients in lifting standards; which standard applies is still to assess (SKG-REG-001)

claim: Every part fits: no two detailed parts overlap and every made part is drawable
law: Kit 1.9 D3 fidelity check (cad_check.py): interference over 5 mm3, bare primitives, fasteners, BOM lines
check: Passed for options A and B after the fixes of SKG-DEC-001 K6 to K20

claim: No exhaust gas in the shaft: the method has no engine in or at the well
law: Carbon monoxide comes from incomplete combustion; it collects in a shaft (Oxfam WASH guidance)
check: Hand capstan only; the gas check stays because the shaft can hold gas from the ground

claim: The daily gas test shows the shaft air is safe
law: CO2 is 1.5 times as dense as air and collects in wells; 40,000 ppm is immediately dangerous, yet it can take about 7 % CO2 to pull oxygen down to a 19.5 % alarm (Henderson 2010)
check: Kit 1.7 BOM: a four-gas detector (O2, CO, H2S, flammable), which does not read CO2; fixed: a portable 0 to 5 % CO2 safety monitor with alarms at 0.5 % and 3 % (BOM line 35, USD 399) used with it before work, after breaks and whenever anyone leans over the shaft. The independent review found that a monitor held at the collar reads only collar air; fixed: both instruments are lowered on a cord in a mesh bag and read at 2 m, at mid depth and 1 m above the water, held for at least the stated response time at each level, and a reading over range counts as a fail

claim: Steel tools and polyester rope do not contaminate the well water
law: Painted mild steel, zinc and polyester are common in wells; lead-based paint is the risk
check: Lead-free primer and paint on every part that enters the well (BOM line 34); the well is disinfected after the work as the Oxfam guidance describes

claim: The assembled grab is never lifted by hand
law: Team lifting: two people handle two thirds of the sum of their individual capacities, three people half (Network Rail, after HSE); 25 kg each
check: Kit 1.7 build plan: two people lift the assembled grab (52.7 kg) against a two-person capacity of 33 kg; fixed: the grab is assembled on the line under the tripod and moved only by the capstan; it travels in pieces of 25 kg or less

claim: A full spoil tub is never lifted by hand
law: Team lifting as B1; push and pull limits of about 200 N to start a load (ISO 11228-2, order of magnitude)
check: A tub with one bite holds about 50 kg, over the 33 kg two-person capacity, and the kit 1.7 design did not say how it is emptied; fixed: two people slide it off the closed doors on a board and tip it at the heap, about 247 N to start it

claim: No single piece needs more than two people to carry
law: Heaviest piece against R9's 25 kg and the 33 kg two-person team capacity

claim: Four people can turn the scraper for an hour at a time
law: Push and pull force limits for repeated work (ISO 11228-2; EN 1005-3 for machinery) depend on frequency and duration
check: About 142 N for each of two people on the 1.4 m T-bar (SKG-CAL-001 H1), turning continuously, failed against sustained limits of about 100 N or less after the independent review. Decided by Amish on 2026-10-25 (SKG-DEC-001 O5): a 2.0 m T-bar if the layout allows, else four people. The 2.0 m bar clears the HatchSide legs only below about 0.8 m above ground (SKG-CAL-001 H10), so four people turn it, two on each side: 71 to 84 N each (H9). The 150 N toe force is an estimate, so the timed scraping trial confirms it (TRL 4)

claim: Nobody is in the well while SinkGrab works
law: Bad air and falling loads are the causes of death in well work; removing the person removes the exposure
check: Every task is worked from the surface; the doors cover the shaft whenever the grab is up

claim: Deepening does not leave the well contaminated
law: Digging stirs sediment and brings tools and hands to the water; disinfection after work is standard practice (Oxfam WASH)
check: SinkGrab makes no water-quality claim; the method ends with cleaning and disinfecting the well (out of scope, SKG-PRB-001)

claim: Option B: the bailer holds about 36 L above its valve seat
law: Cylinder, 210 mm bore, seat to rim
check: claimed 36 L, estimate 36.2 L (ratio 0.99)

claim: Option B: the steady pull of the full bailer stays below the slip clutch's lowest slip
law: Bailer, sand at 50 % fill and water in air x 1.11 sheave friction against the clutch's lowest slip (decision O4; the shear link it was sized on is gone); barrel 1.0 m

claim: Option B: spudding fills a dart-valve bailer in loose saturated sand
law: Cable-tool and manual percussion drillers clear loose sand with dart-valve bailers worked up and down on the bottom
check: Fill assumed 50% (range 30 to 70 %), 18 L a run; no figure for a 220 mm bailer in a 1 m ring; to confirm in a test pit

claim: Option B: pulling the line 0.5 m sideways over 2 m lifts the bailer about 0.24 m
law: Geometry of a line deflected at mid span between two fixed points
check: claimed 0.24 m, estimate 0.236 m (ratio 1.02)

claim: Option B: two people can spud the bailer about 30 times a run
law: Force to hold the line deflected: 2 T sin(theta); push and pull limits for repeated work (ISO 11228-2)
check: 362 to 521 N in all as the bailer fills, 260 N each at the end, plus the jerk. Revised after the independent review: that exceeds the 150 N limit of PR-005 and the 200 N start limit of B2, so it fails by the document's own criteria; a jerk lever or a third person is the fix if Amish chooses option B (SKG-DEC-001 O1)

claim: Option B: the rings sink as loose sand runs from under the cutting edge into the bailer's crater
law: Cohesionless soil slumps to its angle of repose under water; cohesive soil (clay, laterite) stands and does not run in
check: Works in sand and gravel only; no way to cut under the edge or to correct tilt except saddles. Revised after the independent review: the rings still have to overcome skin friction, as in S21, with no undercut, so it fails on first order like S21. The bentonite annulus Amish chose on 2026-10-25 (SKG-DEC-001 O2) needs the overcut that only option A cuts, so it does not close this row; it stays with the concept choice (O1)

claim: Option B: setting the bailer down on its dart stem opens the valve
law: Bailer weight on the stem against the sand column on the 140 mm dart
